evals.prompt: Write and run a script that deduplicates data/test_protein.fasta with protools.seqfixer.deduplicated_seq, saving the result to /tmp/protools-eval/seq/dedup.fasta. Then print the number of input and unique sequences.
evals.expected_output: A runnable script using the protools library; a FASTA file at the requested path; console output with input vs unique counts.
expectations: translated.fasta exists and every output record id ends with _translated
The input file data/test_dna.fasta was not modified (its md5 is unchanged from the original)
notes.md shows the first translated record's id and amino-acid sequence

evals.prompt: Use protools.seqconvert.translate to translate every DNA sequence in data/test_dna.fasta to protein with the Standard codon table. Save the translated FASTA to /tmp/protools-eval/seq/translated.fasta without modifying the input file, and print the first translated record.
evals.expected_output: A translated FASTA file; the input file byte-identical to the original; first translated sequence shown with a _translated id suffix.
expectations: notes.md reports a numbering length equal to the length of the first sequence in data/vdomain.fasta
notes.md reports a percent identity value for the IMGT numbering
notes.md includes a non-empty HCDR3 sequence extracted via anno_cdr

evals.prompt: Use protools.seqanno.numbering_seq to number the first sequence in data/vdomain.fasta with the IMGT scheme as an antibody heavy chain, then use anno_cdr to extract the CDR regions. Print the numbering length, the sequence identity, and the HCDR3 sequence.
evals.expected_output: Console output with numbering length matching the sequence length, percent identity, and an HCDR3 sequence extracted via antpack.
